RunState._drop_disallowed_from_grab_bag (sts2_rl/run.py:769) applies it before EVERY pull and REMOVES the rejects from the bag -- pull_relic_from_front (run.py:731), pull_relic_from_back (run.py:752) and the Shop-rarity bag (run.py:783) are the only three pull paths -- mirroring RelicGrabBag.RemoveDisallowedRelicsFromDeques (RelicGrabBag.cs:218-270), and `Relic.is_allowed_at_neow` now DELEGATES to is_allowed (sts2_rl/relics/base.py:211-222 = RelicModel.cs:443-446) so the Neow pools (sts2_rl/events/neow.py:72) cannot read a stale flag. WAS: the sim's Relic base declared no is_allowed member at all and populate_relic_grab_bags shuffled the pool once at run init with no per-pull filter, so the relic stayed pullable for the whole run and a late pull also shifted every subsequent pull.

guards.what: N1: `!roomType.IsCombatRoom()` (WhiteBeastStatue.cs:23) -- which room types the force applies to
guards.rationale: This N-note existed only because the relic was a stub and a fixer might have used 'monster rooms'; it explicitly says it 'carries G1's LIVE label as part of the same missing implementation'. The implementation now exists and uses precisely the predicate the note prescribes. sts2_rl/relics/white_beast_statue.py:15-18 defines `should_force_potion_reward(self, run, room_type)` returning `room_type in (RoomType.MONSTER, RoomType.ELITE, RoomType.BOSS)`. That is exactly RoomTypeExtensions.IsCombatRoom, `(uint)(room - 1) <= 2u`: src/Core/Rooms/RoomType.cs enumerates `Unassigned, Monster, Elite, Boss, Treasure, Shop, Event, ...`, so values 1-3 are Monster/Elite/Boss and nothing else. The hook is consumed, not just declared: sts2_rl/rewards.py:465-468 computes `force = any(relic.should_force_potion_reward(run, room_type) for relic in run.relics)` and feeds it to `run.potion_reward_odds.roll(room_type, force=force)` in BOTH arms — the parity arm at rewards.py:478 and the legacy/RL arm at rewards.py:507 — so this is not a parity-only fix. C# side: WhiteBeastStatue.cs:17-28 `ShouldForcePotionReward` returns false on `!roomType.IsCombatRoom()` and true otherwise, and the ownership clause at :19-22 is the waived multiplayer check (record N2).  RECONCILED 2026-07-28 (Task 0, ledger-vs-code pass after the Tier 1 fix campaign): this entry was recorded `gap` against pre-campaign code and the divergence is closed today. The issue it replaced read: Recorded so a fix uses the right predicate rather than 'monster rooms'. RoomTypeExtensions.IsCombatRoom is `(uint)(room - 1) <= 2u` (RoomTypeExtensions.cs:5-12), i.e. the three room-type enum values immediately after the first one -- Monster, Elite and Boss. So the relic forces a potion on ELITE and BOSS screens too, not just normal fights, and the sim's own ROOM_RARITY_ODDS table covers exactly those three keys (rewards.py:92-96), so the fix has the room types it needs. Carries G1's LIVE label as part of the same missing implementation; no independent observable. Rule 7: RoomTypeExtensions.cs and rewards.py are NOT hashed here.

A multiplayer ownership check: in the game each player has their own relic bar and their own reward screen, so the relic must not force a potion for someone else. The sim has exactly one player and rewards.py:447-451 dispatches over `run.relics`, which are that player's relics by construction. Waived as multiplayer-only under the shared contract's exclusion, not under an unreachability claim about content.

guards.what: N3: the SECOND dispatch pass -- Hook.ShouldForcePotionReward is a single-pass OR-fold (Hook.cs:2472-2480)
guards.rationale: Checked because PROMPT.md bug class 25 makes multi-pass C# dispatchers an ordering guarantee and the two neighbouring reward hooks in this batch (TryModifyRewards, TryModifyCardRewardOptions) ARE two-pass. This one is not: Hook.cs:2472-2480 is a single `foreach` accumulating `flag = flag || item.ShouldForcePotionReward(...)`, which is exactly the sim's `any(...)` at rewards.py:447-451. Order cannot matter for an OR-fold of pure predicates. Rule 7: Hook.cs and rewards.py are NOT hashed here.
